tagline: Through the shortgrass, past the towns a coal railroad left.
intro: NM 39 comes south through the Kiowa National Grassland, shortgrass prairie nearly all of it leased for grazing cattle, and on through Roy and Mosquero toward the Canadian River. Small mission churches stand along the road from Solano to Gallegos.

Roy and Mosquero grew up on the Dawson Railway, built in 1902 from Tucumcari to the coal fields at Dawson. When the rails came up after mid-century, Roy started a long decline. The road ends at Logan, a town born when the Rock Island bridged the Canadian River, with Ute Lake just to the west.

moments.title: Mills Canyon
moments.text: Six miles west of Mills the grassland drops 700 feet into the red-rock canyon of the Canadian River, where Melvin Mills once kept an apple orchard on the floor.

moments.title: Roy
moments.text: Roy moved two miles east to meet the Dawson Railway, and its more than 40 city blocks still show the size it reached before the rails came up.

moments.title: Mosquero
moments.text: A water stop on the Dawson line whose name is Spanish for swarm of flies, and which once made dry ice from the carbon dioxide of local gas wells.

sources.label: New Mexico True, La Frontera del Llano
